facts.text: The producers' brief for Skyscraper was reportedly simply "Die Hard, but with Anna Nicole Smith." Writer Bill Applegate then added the Shakespeare-quoting villain.
Villain Fairfax is played by Charles M. Huber, a German actor who later became a politician. Den of Geek notes he went on to serve in German politics.
Charles M. Huber (villain Fairfax) played police superintendent Henry Johnson on German TV's Der Alte from 1986 to 1997, then sat in the German Bundestag for the CDU from 2013 to 2017.
Writer Joseph John Barmettler wrote the first draft, which the producers found unsatisfactory. Bill Applegate then rewrote it, and Barmettler reportedly removed his name from the finished film.
Entertainment Tonight visited the set to profile Anna Nicole Smith, but she slurred her lines so badly that none of the footage was usable. The segment was scrapped.
Production began in August 1995 for PM Entertainment, whose name is a mash-up of founders Richard Pepin and Joseph Merhi's surnames.
Smith's footage was so rough that she had to get sober and return to re-record nearly all her dialogue in post-production (ADR).
Co-writer Bill Applegate started on PM Entertainment films as a lowly second second assistant director. This was his path to writing Tiger Heart (1996) and then this film.
Director Raymond Martino was fired when dailies disappointed the producers. PM Entertainment co-founder Joseph Merhi stepped in to direct reshoots and oversee ADR.
The film's tagline promised 'Eighty-six floors of action-packed terror!' IMDb's goofs list notes the movie only ever shows the 26th floor as the building's top.
Writer Bill Applegate says producer Joseph Merhi was so unhappy with the finished cut that he took his name off it, and shot missing pickups himself to make the story coherent.
Shot in Los Angeles at 444 S. Flower Street downtown, plus the Hyatt Regency Hotel in Long Beach.
Anna Nicole Smith's billionaire husband J. Howard Marshall died on August 4, 1995, just as this film's shoot began. She reportedly collapsed with convulsions in New York and was hospitalized.
Deron McBee (Leidermeier) was an original American Gladiators star as 'Malibu', and later played the four-armed Motaro in Mortal Kombat Annihilation (1997).
The kid on the Shining-style big-wheel trike is played by Anna Nicole Smith's real son, Daniel Smith. He died in 2006, aged 20, five months before his mother.
Star Richard Steinmetz (Gordon Wink) hosted the Miss World pageant for four straight years, including broadcasts from South Africa and India, and coaches high school football.
Insurance rules kept the lead actors off the building's exterior at height, so the stunt coordinator performed most of the high-altitude wire work himself.
Calvin Levels, who plays Hakim, was nominated for the 1984 Tony Award for Best Actor (Play) for Broadway's 'Open Admissions' before ending up in a PM Entertainment B-movie.
Den of Geek said the film was made on roughly the budget of an episode of the soap Dynasty, and noted its stunts were impressive even if the editing and fights were weak.
Jonathan Fuller (Jacques) was chosen in a nationwide search in 1984 to be the first actor to play Jesus in the Crystal Cathedral's Passion Play, 'The Glory of Easter'.
Co-star Branko Cikatic, a Croatian kickboxer, won the first-ever K-1 World Grand Prix in 1993. He was also an associate producer on this movie.
A reviewer at The Nics Periment said the action looks like Die Hard and Clear and Present Danger staged 'on a tenth of the budget', yet still rated it 'so bad it's good'.
The same Los Angeles office building served as the villains' HQ in Anna Nicole Smith's earlier PM Entertainment action film To the Limit (1995).
Den of Geek notes the film restages Die Hard ideas on the cheap. Where Bruce Willis improvised a bomb, Anna Nicole Smith's Carrie Wink sets wastebasket fires.
In Germany, the VHS from Highlight Video was cut by about 9 minutes for violence to get an FSK-18 rating. An uncut disc was only due in 2024.
A cleaned-up TV edition removes every sequence with nudity to meet broadcast standards, a big cut for a movie that sold itself on Anna Nicole Smith.
The UK video release was cut by 56 seconds, trimming shots of Carrie being groped in an attack scene and her stabbing the attacker's leg with a letter opener.
The UK DVD cover is plastered with pull-quotes that sell the nudity, including 'Ms. Smith gets her kit off' and 'Bra busting!', per Den of Geek and JoBlo.
India's 2004 release was trimmed to 78 minutes, with large parts of Anna Nicole Smith's sex scenes missing, and the 4:3 picture was changed to 1.78:1.
Saturday Night Live's 2000 sketch 'FANatic', written and directed by Paul Thomas Anderson, had Molly Shannon as Anna Nicole Smith. IMDb lists it as spoofing this film.
Stunt coordinator Cole McKay is credited first in the end credits, a nod to how much the movie leans on its stunts.
PM Entertainment, the studio behind this film, was sold to Harvey Entertainment in 2000 for $6.5 million in cash plus about $1.45 million in stock.
The 2018 Dwayne Johnson thriller Skyscraper shares this film's title and building-under-siege premise. This earlier movie is credited as being referenced in it.
